nodes.label: Homepage Running Order
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a running order and nothing else: every section is a template part so any one can be reworked in isolation.

nodes.label: Tradition Doors Above Packages
nodes.rationale: The doors reframe what the visitor thinks they are shopping for before a price appears; once someone compares $350 to $1,000 the pilgrimage framing is gone and the site competes on cost with all of Thamel.

nodes.label: Money Explainer Before Lineage
nodes.rationale: For an international wire transfer to Nepal, uncertainty about money is a sharper objection than uncertainty about quality.

nodes.label: How a Place Is Confirmed Section
Check Us Before You Pay Us Section
Lineage Section
nodes.rationale: Lineage instead of testimonials, because there are none yet and the theme does not invent them or borrow the parent company's.

nodes.label: Elementor Document Takeover Check
nodes.rationale: Pages used to fall through to index.php with no title, width constraint or wrapper. When Elementor owns the document it takes over the content and the tk-page__banner title band is suppressed so the page's own hero is first on screen.

nodes.label: Parikrama Line Rail
nodes.rationale: One brass hairline drawn by scroll makes the homepage read as one continuous walk rather than stacked sections, and each marker is a real link, so the ornament also navigates.

nodes.label: Reduced-Motion and Narrow-Viewport Modes
nodes.rationale: Under prefers-reduced-motion the line is drawn fully and held still rather than removed, because it is a wayfinding device as much as an ornament. Below 1200px it is hidden entirely.

nodes.label: Rail Built in JS, Not Shipped in Markup
nodes.rationale: A page with no JavaScript should not carry a dead ornament, and the markers must be derived from whichever sections actually rendered: doors, verify and guides all remove themselves when they have nothing to show.

nodes.label: Five Static-Hero Gates
nodes.rationale: The five media queries deciding scrub vs still are declared twice and must match character for character. When they drift nothing throws: one side hides the stage while the other downloads a video nobody sees, or CSS un-hides a stage JS never armed and the visitor gets a blank multi-viewport hero.

nodes.label: Retired Package Details Meta Box
nodes.rationale: Retired in favour of inc/package-admin.php. Unhooking the save handler is the part that matters: both systems own price_from and best_months and disagree about shape (text string vs list of month integers), so whichever ran last would corrupt the other's data on every update. The functions stay defined so nothing that calls them fatals.

nodes.label: tk_get_package_options
nodes.rationale: Several widgets each ran get_posts with posts_per_page -1, hydrating a full WP_Post and priming meta and term caches for every package to read one column, twice per front-end render. This queries the needed columns, caches in a transient and memoises for the rest of the request.

nodes.label: TouristTrip Schema
nodes.rationale: TouristTrip is the type that actually describes what is sold. Product alone described a fourteen day pilgrimage over a 5,630 m pass the same way it would describe a kettle. Everything comes from a field: a property with no value is omitted rather than guessed at, because structured data is a claim made to a machine that will repeat it.

nodes.label: Filters as Real Links, Not JS Tabs
nodes.rationale: Real URLs make every filtered view shareable, bookmarkable and crawlable, and the catalogue still filters on a connection too poor to run a script, which is a real condition for much of this audience. Traditions with no packages are not offered, because a filter leading to an empty page is worse than one fewer filter.

nodes.label: Package FAQ Template Part
nodes.rationale: Built on details/summary so it needs no JavaScript and the browser handles keyboard support; the same questions are handed to schema so what a search engine sees and what a visitor reads cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: Render Nothing When There Is Nothing To Say
nodes.rationale: Live pages carried a grey block with no content under the Tour Overview heading, which reads as a broken page rather than an empty one, and was flagged in review for exactly that.

nodes.label: Designed Still Hero
nodes.rationale: Not a fallback apology but a composed layout over the ending frame, and what most of this audience sees because most of this traffic is Indian and Nepali mobile. It carries the real heading and actions so the page works even if the video never loads or was never added.

nodes.label: Horse Year Merit Line Held Behind a Flag
nodes.rationale: Sources give the Horse Year multiplier as thirteen, some as twelve. The line does not ship until the operator confirms which figure their own tradition uses: getting religious detail wrong on a pilgrimage site is worse than saying nothing.

nodes.label: Licence and Registration Line
nodes.rationale: Registration numbers come from the Customizer and an unset one is simply omitted: a site whose central trust argument is 'check our numbers' cannot print a placeholder where a number belongs.

nodes.label: Theme Directory Capitalisation Matters
nodes.rationale: WordPress resolves the theme by directory name and most hosts run a case-sensitive filesystem, so a lowercase trip-kailash directory will not activate.

nodes.label: TK_FORM_RECIPIENT Fixed in Code
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not configurable from the page: reading the recipient from the form let anyone submit their own destination address and use the site as a mail relay.

nodes.label: Version Constant and style.css Must Match
nodes.rationale: TRIP_KAILASH_VERSION is what busts browser caches for CSS and JS, so it must stay in sync with the Version: header in style.css.

nodes.label: bin/lint-php.sh Pre-Push Gate
nodes.rationale: A WordPress theme has no build step, so nothing catches a PHP parse error before it reaches the server, where it becomes a white screen on the live site. CI runs the same check pinned to PHP 8.4 to match production.

nodes.label: Page Layouts Live in the Database
nodes.rationale: Layouts are stored as Elementor data in the database, not as templates in the repo. A widget's PHP controls what it can render; the live page decides what it does render.

nodes.label: .htaccess Not in Version Control
nodes.rationale: Because .htaccess is not tracked, the canonical domain redirect is handled in inc/seo.php instead.

nodes.label: SVG Wave Hero Bottom
nodes.rationale: The wave fills with the page background colour and scales with preserveAspectRatio none; the section still looks good without it, so it degrades gracefully. It required changing .tk-hero-video overflow from hidden to visible.

hyperedges.label: FAQ answers reach visitor and search engine from one source
hyperedges.description: faq.php renders tk_package('faq') and hands the same question/answer pairs to tk_register_page_faqs; a request-scoped global carries them to tk_build_page_schema, which merges them with the faqs post meta and emits FAQPage in the footer. The point of the loop is that rendered copy and structured data cannot drift.

hyperedges.label: Five hero gates declared twice and policed by a script
hyperedges.description: The same five media queries decide scrub vs still in home.css and in hero-scrub.js. hero.php's markup switches on the same condition via tk-hero--scrub / tk-hero--still-only. Nothing throws on drift, so check-hero-gates.py compares the two declarations character for character.

hyperedges.label: Cached package option list and its invalidation hooks
hyperedges.description: tk_get_package_options replaces per-widget unbounded get_posts calls with one column query cached for twelve hours and memoised per request; save_post, trashed_post, untrashed_post and deleted_post all flush it, but only for pilgrimage_package. Widgets such as Featured Packages still run their own uncached queries alongside it.
